newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM designate Chavalit vows to focus on economy.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM designate Chavalit vows to focus on economy.

text.p: Thailand's newly-appointed prime minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Tuesday the top priority of his administration will be to improve the nation's slowing economy.

Chavalit told foreign journalists in his first interview since his appointment to Thailand's top job that he would name a group of experts led by respected economist Amnuay Viravan as finance minister to help revive the lagging economy.
"My top priority is the economy. I see my role as providing leadership...to accomplish this I shall bring together the best talents in the country," Chavalit said.
Chavalit's New Aspiration Party (NAP) won a slim two-seat victory over the Democrats in the November 17 general election.

Chavalit, who was officially named Thailand's 22nd prime minister late on Monday by royal decree, has formed a six-party coalition that will command a comfortable majority with 221 seats in the 393-seat parliament.
"Thailand is now facing a serious crisis -- a crisis of confidence rather than a crisis of ability," he said.
"Confidence will be restored when there is a perception that the right people are in the right jobs and that they are working together as a united team for the benefit of their country."
During his election campaign Chavalit had pledged to appoint an economic team made up of several non-elected experts to help reverse the economic slowdown.
Private economists project that the Thai economy will expand at a 10-year low of six to seven percent this year.
Chavalit said Amnuay, a finance minister in 1980-1, would also be deputy prime minister in charge of economic affairs.

He said Narongchai Akrasanee, chairman of General Finance and Securities Plc, will take over the commerce portfolio, and Somphob Amatayakul, president of Saha Union Plc, will be named deputy industry minister.

He said he was confident the economic team could solve the nation's problems, adding the first priority would be to narrow the current account deficit which amounted to about 8.1 percent of gross domestic product in 1995 -- the highest in five years.
"We need to cut the current account deficit. We have to accelerate exports, bring export competitiveness up... We also need to increase domestic savings," said Chavalit.
Chavalit said he and his New Aspiration Party had solved all the major problems with the second-largest coalition member, Chart Pattana Party, regarding the sharing of cabinet posts.

In the past eight days since the election, the Thai bourse has been jumpy on talks of delays in negotiations over how to divide the cabinet ministries. On Tuesday the market ended down nearly one percent at 958.14 points.

Coalition sources had said the Chart Pattana party had demanded more voice in economic issues, saying the party had qualified elected politicians and the government should not rely so much on non-elected experts like Amnuay.
But Chavalit said the problems had been worked out.
He expects to present a list of cabinet members to King Bhumibol Adulyadej in the next few days. He and his cabinet should be sworn in on December 1, one of his top aides said.
